recipes.name: Traditional White Bread
ingredients_raw: 2.5 cups warm water (110 degrees F/45 degrees C)

steps.text: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water in a large bowl. Stir in 2 cups flour, lard, and salt. Stir in the remaining flour, 1/2 cup at a time, mixing well after each addition. When the dough comes together, turn it out onto a lightly floured surface and knead until smooth and elastic, about 8 minutes.
Lightly oil a large bowl, then place the dough in the bowl and turn to coat with oil. Cover with a damp cloth and let rise in a warm place until doubled in volume, about 1 hour.

Deflate the dough and turn it out onto a lightly floured surface. Divide the dough into two equal pieces and form into loaves. Place the loaves into the prepared pans, cover with a damp cloth, and let rise until doubled in volume, about 40 minutes.

Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Place bread in the preheated oven and lower the temperature to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Bake until the top is golden brown and the bottom of the loaf sounds hollow when tapped, about 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Traditional White Bread
raw_recipe.description: A delicious white bread recipe with a very light center with crunchy crust. You may substitute butter or vegetable oil for the lard if you wish.

review.reviewBody: I absolutely LOVE this bread recipe. I found it a year ago and never used another one since. I personally like to take the bread out 5 minutes before and brush melted butter on the top and let it finish the lasr 5 minutes of cooking. Thanks for this wonderful bread recipe!

This recipe was so simplistic and the results were beyond my expectations. I used my KitchenAid mixer with the dough hook attachment to form the dough and halved the recipe. The instructions were straight-forward and the bread was "store-bought" quality. The only substitution I made was using a whole wheat bread flour. Thanks for sharing your delicious recipe.

I made it once and it turned out ok for the first time I made homemade bread in over 20 years. Then I tried again. My lack of preparation ended up a good thing. My phone died, but I wanted bread for dinner. And then I was out of white sugar. Well when I was done it turned out to be the best homemade bread I ever had. I substituted light brown sugar for white sugar. Then I forgot to take the butter out of the fridge. So I added it later and it was melted instead of soft. I used salted sweet cream butter and left out the salt. I added the melted butter just before turning it out on the floured surface. Then I kneaded it to get the butter fully incorporated, then I put it into the oiled bowl and let it rise for an hour. Then I split it into two then flatten them out and roll it into two loaves and rise again then baked it for 30 minutes . The best I ever had much less ever made. Everyone in the house said it was amazing.

I know everyone says that a recipe they use is the best but, this really is the best! Started using it during the Pandemic and here it is, still here and about to pick up a partner, bird flu and still using it! One thing I do for the past year or so is I use half a recipe, throw the instant dry yeast in a measuring cup with the sugar and warm water, let it foam for 5 minutes, add the oil then dump it into the bucket of my bread machine, add 3 cups of bread flour, the salt, set it on DOUGH cycle and let it go. I take it out when risen and dump onto a lightly floured piece of parchment paper on my countertop, deflate it, shape it into a loaf and put into an oiled or greased bread pan, cover it with oiled plastic wrap. Let it rise till it breaches the top of the pan, heat oven as the recipe says and let it go for a half hour. Perfect every single time. Perfect loaf without all the hassle. I don’t bake it in the bread machine because bread machine bread sucks but if you let the bread machine do the work and you do the shaping and baking, it is perfection!

So easy and the first bread recipe that actually turned out twice so far. 6 mins on #2 setting on my Kitchenaid instead of kneading. Worked perfect both times. Brushed with butter 10 mins before done and then when done. Used butter instead of lard. Great recipe!

Amazing & simple, no fail, white bread recipe!! I used butter instead of lard, kept everything else the same(including the sugar/salt). We also melted butter on top of the loaf 5min before it came out of the oven. Easiest way is to use the stick of butter to rub the bread all over...like how you might butter corn. We made 2- 12x6 loaves(~4" high when done)& used the whole stick to butter the tops. The kids couldn't get enough!! They said they preferred this to their favorite natures own butterbread...that's a HUGE compliment!! Thanks for the great recipe!!!

Great recipe! This was my first time making a loaf of bread. I didn't have powdered milk, so used 2 1/2 cups of whole milk at 110°F. I used about half of the amount of salt and added 1 more tablespoon of sugar, and used bread flour. I only made these minor changes because I knew I didnt want 2 loaves of bread and already planned to make some rolls, but I like for them to taste a certain way. I cooked it in my Pullman loaf pan, with the lid. Also, I reserved the last 1/2 cup of flour and just worked it in when I kneaded it (just because I know my home is pretty humid, and I don't usually need all of the flour recipes call for. I used alll 6 1/2 cups! The other half of the dough made some wonderful dinner rolls/sliders!

I changed it up completely as from experience noted there was way too much salt and sugar and even yeast. I used 4½ cups or 600g bread flour, 7gm yeast, 7gm sugar, 7gm salt, 24gm canola oil and 678gm warm water (33⁰C). 1st rise was about 20-30 minutes so I didn't over prove it and second rise about 50 minutes. I also find measuring by weight is better than by using cup and spoon measures. Instant dry yeast is better added to flour too rather than to water.

Great bread, lasts a long time in a ziplock. I also brushed it with butter, used olive oil instead of lard, less salt and then baked for just 20 minutes. I put everything but the flour in the starter then poured everything in the mixer at once... will cut back on the sugar for my next batch. 
-740 g bread flour
-610g water
-15g yeast
-35g olive oil
-45g sugar
-10g salt

Highly recommend this recipe. I proofed the yeast first and man did this dough rise! Rose great again in the loaf pans. Delicious. It made the best grill cheese sandwich! For vegan option used plant based butter. Followed measurements as written.

My whole family, friends and neighbors love this bread! I just substituted the lard for butter because I was out of lard and it was perfect! This made 3 regular sized loaves in my loaf pans for me also. When I tried to only do 2 the first time, they were way too big and looking crazy haha but 3 was perfect! Also, all purpose flour is ok, but if you really want the bread to have structure and not fall apart, then use bread flour or a higher protein flour and make sure to knead enough and rise enough to build that gluten! 😊

Hands down the best recipe I’ve tried. Lard is the magic ingredient for sure. I’ve tried so many other recipes that all turned out dry. Not this one. It’s soft and chewy. Better than store bought for sure. Thank you for sharing!!

This was so easy to do. Just followed the instructions and while the dough was rising went and did other things. Came back, put the bread in the oven and done. 2 loaves of fresh bread. I did rub butter all over the top when fresh out of oven but that's a personal taste thing. Will definitely be keeping this one.
Absolutely the best bread recipe I've ever made, it's so yummy. Thank you.
I used butter in place of the lard and it turned out great. I've been looking to get bavk into making sandwich bread and this might end up being my go-to recipe.
I hate baking but I need to eat food with ingredients i can pronounce. This recipe is so easy to follow and comes out perfect every time
My only modification was 1/4 tsp more salt.
regardless of 1/2x 1x or 2x, it says "lighly grease two 9x5 loaf pans"
Great
It was so easy, it made the house smell so good! The bread itself tasted delicious! Some recipes aren't so clear for instructions. Im going to make some homemade cinnamon rolls! Yuuuuumy!
